title: evidence/dup_groups.py
body:
"""Group a jscpd report's clone pairs by where their two files sit, and list the stand-check families.
usage: python3 dup_groups.py {jscpd-report.json} {repo_root}
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import sys

rep, root = sys.argv[1:3]
root = os.path.realpath(root)
j = json.load(open(rep, encoding='utf-8'))


def rel(p):
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(p), root).replace('\\', '/')


def cls(p):
    if p.startswith('tests/blitz-tests/tests/'):
        base = p.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
        if '/common/' in p or '/session_common/' in p or '/fixtures/' in p:
            return 'bt-shared'
        return 'bt-stand' if base.startswith('stand_') else 'bt-other'
    if p.startswith('examples/seven_guis/tests/'):
        return 'sg-tests'
    if '/tests/' in '/' + p:
        return 'other-tests'
    return 'src'


groups = collections.Counter()
glines = collections.Counter()
per_file = collections.Counter()
stand_pairs = []
for d in j['duplicates']:
    a, b = rel(d['firstFile']['name']), rel(d['secondFile']['name'])
    n = d['lines']
    k = tuple(sorted((cls(a), cls(b))))
    groups[k] += 1
    glines[k] += n
    if k == ('bt-stand', 'bt-stand') or 'bt-shared' in k and all(c in ('bt-stand', 'bt-shared') for c in k):
        stand_pairs.append((n, f"{a}:{d['firstFile']['start']}-{d['firstFile']['end']}", f"{b}:{d['secondFile']['start']}-{d['secondFile']['end']}"))
        per_file[a] += n
        per_file[b] += n

print('pairs by class (pairs, lines):')
for k in sorted(groups, key=lambda k: -glines[k]):
    print(f'  {k[0]} x {k[1]}: {groups[k]} pairs, {glines[k]} lines')
print(f'stand-check pairs: {len(stand_pairs)}, lines {sum(p[0] for p in stand_pairs)}')
print('files by stand-pair lines (top 30):')
for f, n in per_file.most_common(30):
    print(f'  {n:5d} {f}')
print('stand pairs, largest 60:')
for n, a, b in sorted(stand_pairs, reverse=True)[:60]:
    print(f'  {n:4d} {a}  ~  {b}')

"""What the stand-setup fold must leave as it was, read against the commit the chunk starts from.
usage: python3 fold_guard.py {base_sha}

Over tests/blitz-tests/tests/ (every .rs file, the shared modules included):
  files     — the same file paths at the base and in the working tree (nothing renamed, merged or split);
  tests     — per file, the same #[test] function names, in a sorted list;
  ignores   — per file, the same count of #[ignore] attributes;
  literals  — over the stand_*.rs files and the three shared modules together, the same SET of distinct
              string literals: a moved assertion or setup line keeps its literals, a collapsed copy keeps
              the set, and a new or dropped message reads as a difference.
Prints one line per failing reading (counts and file names only) and a last line
`fold guard: PASS` or `fold guard: FAIL`; exits 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

BASE = sys.argv[1]
DIR = 'tests/blitz-tests/tests'
SHARED = ('common/', 'session_common/', 'fixtures/')


def lex(text):
    """The text with comments removed and every string literal replaced by a marker, and the literals."""
    out, literals, i, n = [], [], 0, len(text)
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if text.startswith('//', i):
            j = text.find('\n', i)
            i = n if j < 0 else j
            continue
        if text.startswith('/*', i):
            depth, i = 1, i + 2
            while i < n and depth:
                if text.startswith('/*', i):
                    depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
                elif text.startswith('*/', i):
                    depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
                else:
                    i += 1
            continue
        m = re.match(r'b?r(#*)"', text[i:])
        if m and (i == 0 or not (text[i - 1].isalnum() or text[i - 1] == '_')):
            close = '"' + m.group(1)
            start = i + m.end()
            end = text.find(close, start)
            end = n if end < 0 else end
            literals.append(text[start:end])
            out.append(' "S" ')
            i = end + len(close)
            continue
        if c == '"' or (c == 'b' and text.startswith('b"', i)):
            start = i + (2 if c == 'b' else 1)
            j = start
            while j < n and text[j] != '"':
                j += 2 if text[j] == '\\' else 1
            literals.append(text[start:j])
            out.append(' "S" ')
            i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == "'":
            m = re.match(r"'(\\.[^']*|[^\\'])'", text[i:])
            if m:
                out.append(" 'C' ")
                i += m.end()

    if stand_file(rel):

        work_literals.update(work_lits)

    failures.append(f'literals: +{len(work_literals - base_literals)} -{len(base_literals - work_literals)}')

for line in failures:
    print(line)
print(f'files {len(base_files)} · tests {tests} · literals {len(base_literals)}')
print('fold guard: ' + ('FAIL' if failures else 'PASS'))

"""The stand checks' own duplication reading over a jscpd report, held to a bar.
usage: python3 stand_reading.py {jscpd-report.json} {repo_root} {pairs_bar} {lines_bar}

A pair counts when both of its sides lie in a `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` file or in one of the
three shared modules (`common/`, `session_common/`, `fixtures/` under that directory) — the classes
`dup_groups.py` names bt-stand and bt-shared. The bar holds when the pairs are under `pairs_bar` AND the
lines under `lines_bar`. Prints one line and exits 0 when the bar holds, 1 when it does not.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

rep, root, pairs_bar, lines_bar = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
root = os.path.realpath(root)
report = json.load(open(rep, encoding='utf-8'))
PREFIX = 'tests/blitz-tests/tests/'
SHARED = ('common/', 'session_common/', 'fixtures/')


def rel(path):
    return os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), root).replace('\\', '/')


def stand_side(path):
    if not path.startswith(PREFIX):
        return False
    rest = path[len(PREFIX):]
    return rest.startswith(SHARED) or ('/' not in rest and rest.startswith('stand_'))


pairs = lines = 0
for clone in report['duplicates']:
    if stand_side(rel(clone['firstFile']['name'])) and stand_side(rel(clone['secondFile']['name'])):
        pairs += 1
        lines += clone['lines']
held = pairs < pairs_bar and lines < lines_bar
word = 'PASS' if held else 'FAIL'
print(f'stand reading: {pairs} pairs / {lines} lines · bar under {pairs_bar} / {lines_bar} · stand reading bar: {word}')
sys.exit(0 if held else 1)

body:
"""Duplication (A1) summarizer. usage: python3 sum_dup.py {jscpd-report.json} {repo_root} {out.json}
pct = statistics.total.percentage rounded to 2; top = 10 largest clones (lines desc, ties in report order),
cells {file}:{start line} (repo-relative); split by a `tests` directory segment: both src, both test, or mixed.
"""
import json, os, sys

rep, root, out = sys.argv[1:4]
root = os.path.realpath(root)
j = json.load(open(rep, encoding='utf-8'))
t = j['statistics']['total']


def rel(p):
    p = os.path.realpath(p)
    return os.path.relpath(p, root).replace('\\', '/')


def is_test(p):
    return 'tests' in p.split('/')[:-1]


rows, split = [], {'src': {'pairs': 0, 'lines': 0}, 'test': {'pairs': 0, 'lines': 0}, 'mixed': {'pairs': 0, 'lines': 0}}
for d in j['duplicates']:
    a, b = rel(d['firstFile']['name']), rel(d['secondFile']['name'])
    n = d['lines']
    rows.append([f"{a}:{d['firstFile']['start']}", f"{b}:{d['secondFile']['start']}", n])
    k = 'test' if is_test(a) and is_test(b) else 'src' if not is_test(a) and not is_test(b) else 'mixed'
    split[k]['pairs'] += 1
    split[k]['lines'] += n
top = sorted(enumerate(rows), key=lambda e: (-e[1][2], e[0]))[:10]
o = {'pct': round(t['percentage'], 2), 'duplicated_lines': t['duplicatedLines'], 'total_lines': t['lines'], 'clones': t['clones'],
     'top': [r for _, r in top], 'split': split}
json.dump(o, open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8'), indent=1)
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in o.items() if k != 'top'}))

**Section:** 3. Test Harness Contract
**Change:** ~ decision/shared-stand-tables-in-one-module · except: was «stand_element_ids keeps its own boot (it books the flight), and task_keys, ceiling, component, the cards array and each file's SECRET stay per-file»; now «A helper whose body or failure message differs from the shared one stays in its check; stand_element_ids keeps its own boot; task_keys, ceiling, component, the cards array and SECRET stay per file.»
**Why:** decision/shared-stand-tables-in-one-module: The chunk moved the stand checks' repeated setup into the shared test modules and kept private each helper whose body or failure message differs, an exception the row's except cell must now state.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T04-31-31-wrap/

- **Integration:** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs`, one file per behaviour, depending only on dev-dependencies; the stand checks read the tables and helpers they share from `tests/common/mod.rs` (`mod common;`; a helper whose body or failure message differs from the shared one stays in its check) and the checks that hold a session — the session checks, `stand_settle`, the sixteen driver-action checks `stand_act_*`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `stand_screenshot_repeat`, `stand_requirement_sweep`, `stand_virtual_clock`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording `stand_session_recording` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, `stand_replay` and, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_lint` and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_load_wait` and, since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_snapshot_parts` and the two served-page checks `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` (36 readers, `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` the thirtieth and thirty-first, `stand_act_popup` the thirty-second, `stand_graph` the thirty-third, `stand_actions` the thirty-fourth, `stand_handler_coverage` the thirty-fifth, `stand_seeded_randomness` the thirty-sixth; `stand_mcp_masked`, `password_painted_masked`, `stand_non_lean_tasks` and `password_caret_click` declare none) — what they share from `tests/session_common/mod.rs` (`mod session_common;`: the held session, the driver's call builders `click` · `type_into` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` · `snapshot` · `screenshot` · `screenshot_of` · `lint` · `graph` · `snapshot_part`, the outcome reader `act`, the part reader `part` (a paged snapshot's text, part and count), the shot reader `shot`, the lint reader `linted` (a lint's findings), the graph reader `graphed` (a graph's `UiGraph`), the refusal readers `refused` and `refused_unchanged`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording the recording readers `kept` and the unix-only `mode`, and since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `shot_prefix` (the first 64 base64 characters of a whole-screen shot) — its `replay` removed then for the replay `Check::replay`); and, since 2026-10-19-shared-fixtures, what 32 checks — 24 `stand_*` files (`stand_snapshot_parts` since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_act_select`, `stand_load_wait` since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_lint` since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_act_popup`, `stand_actions`), `font_face_sniffed_source`, `select_interaction`, `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted`, `inert_subtree`, `accessibility_states`, `checkable_change_event` and `text_range_no_change_event` — share from `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (`mod fixtures;`, `#![allow(dead_code)]`: the fixture boot `boot(app, incremental)` with the stand's options `stand::options(incremental)`, `hold(label, app, incremental)` over it, the pages more than one check reads — `password_labelled`, `password_named`, `covered` and `many_items` with its `ITEMS` (read by `stand_snapshot_parts` and `stand_act_spans`) — and the held network stand-in `HeldNet`); none is a test target. Every other file is its own target: `tests/all.rs` is upstream's single-binary target, kept in the manifest at `test = false` and never built — add no `autotests = false` and no second `[[test]]` table (`BlitzTestsTargetsTest`, in the `ci-scripts` leg, pins it). A check that needs a session process starts and stops its own host (its test binary re-run on one `#[ignore]` child, or the package's binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`), bounds every wait, guards the host with kill-and-reap and, holding a session over the socket, is `cfg(unix)`-gated — a check that drives the `escher-session mcp` stdio child (`mcp_server`, `mcp_log`) does it through the shared `Speaker` (piped stdin, stdout read line by line on a thread under a 30 s bound, kill-and-reap in its `Drop`) and is not unix-gated but `mcp_server`'s two command-line comparisons, and a check comparing an MCP tool result against the in-process answer decodes the result's JSON string whole through the one shared session-check helper (un-escaping quotes alone leaves a Windows path's backslashes doubled); since 2026-10-19-session-recording a check that records is `cfg(unix)`-gated item by item, in-process and `mcp` stdio ones included (`mcp_log`'s recorded test), beside an off-unix check that a recording is refused `Unsupported`, which the windows job alone runs; a host ends by itself after its idle expiry, so a check that waits for one watches the state directory — an `attach` or a `status` is an answered request and starts the count again. The seven_guis checks also run the `escher-session` binary once per command as a client and read its stdout, stderr and exit status (`0` · `1` · `2` · `3`) through `tests/common/mod.rs`, which since 2026-10-19-test-splits also states the log checks' fragment once — `Needles` and `stand_needles` (the CRUD stand's id and name needles), `stamped_lines`, `found`, `occurrences`, the unix-only `recorded_needles` and `cells_needles(part)` (part `part`'s author keys of the in-process Cells screen and the middle column-A cell it holds) — called by `host_log` and `mcp_log` alone, `option_needles()` (the needle list of a select's options read from a snapshot), called by the same two, and `graph_needles()` (the component and state names of the UI graph as needles), called by the same two, and `actions_needles()` (the CRUD screen's listed author-key ids holding a `-` as needles), called by the same two, and `coverage_needles()` (the CRUD screen's UI-graph ids and names as needles), called by `host_log` alone; the two flows under `tests/flows/` are POSIX `sh` scripts run by the Rust target `cli_flow` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, a third, `record_checks.sh`, by seven_guis `recording`'s unix-gated `the_committed_checks_are_what_the_binary_records` — assets of a `cargo test` target, not a runner of their own.
